instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Mince the garlic. Drain the artichokes and chop them roughly.
Cook the rigatoni until al dente, following the package time. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Melt the butter in the empty pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells good.
Add the cream cheese and the 1 cup pasta water. Whisk until the cream cheese melts into a smooth sauce.
Stir in the sour cream and the Parmesan. Take the pot off the heat.
Add the pasta, the spinach and half of the artichokes. Stir until the spinach wilts. Stir in the salt and the pepper.
Transfer it to a 9x13 inch baking dish. Top with the mozzarella and the rest of the artichokes.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling. For a browned top, broil on high for 2 to 3 minutes. Watch it closely.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve with the red pepper flakes at the table for anyone who wants heat.
Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat a portion in the microwave with a splash of water.
method_notes: Beyond the Noms is the lead (4.43 from 47): a cream cheese and sour cream sauce thinned with pasta water, with spinach and artichokes folded into rigatoni, topped with mozzarella and baked at 400°F for 15 minutes. It was the only version with both 4.0 and 20+ ratings. Cento tops sautéed spinach and artichokes with ricotta and bakes it 20 to 25 minutes; The Last Food Blog uses a cream cheese and pecorino sauce and bakes it for 30. The lead's amounts are cut to about two thirds for 4 servings, and its red pepper flakes move to the table so the base is mild. Check the Parmesan label if you need it strictly vegetarian, since some Parmesan is made with animal rennet.
